name: Representation Criterion after Deleting a Corner
statement: Let $E$ be ample and let $v$ be a corner whose incident directions form its support $T$. Then $E\setminus\{v\}$ has a representation map exactly when $E$ has a representation map assigning the label $T$ to $v$.
proof: Deleting the corner removes exactly $T$ from the shattered family, so a map with $r(v)=T$ restricts immediately. Conversely, extend a representation map of the deletion by $v\mapsto T$. No other concept agrees with $v$ on $T$: an isometric path to one would have to leave $v$ in a direction outside its corner support. Thus $T$ separates $v$ from every old concept and all new nonclashing conditions hold.
